name: nbody
axis: realistic whole program: f64 arithmetic over an array of mutable structs (O(n^2) pairwise force loop over 5 bodies)

name: spectralnorm
axis: realistic whole program: f64 array indexing in a tight O(n^2) inner loop, plus a small leaf function (A(i,j)) called once per element

name: bitcount
axis: popcnt / clz / ctz

name: bitops
axis: shift / and / or / xor / rotate

name: convert
axis: i32 <-> f64 conversion round trip

name: f64-accum
axis: f64 add/mul — accumulate + globals-cliff probe

name: floatops
axis: sqrt / abs / floor / min / max (no transcendentals)

name: i32-accum
axis: i32 add (wrapping) — trivial accumulate

name: i64-accum
axis: i64 add — trivial accumulate + globals-cliff probe

name: intdivmod
axis: i32 divide + remainder by a loop-varying divisor

name: mixed-width
axis: i32 + i64 + f64 in one loop, explicit `as` casts

name: binsearch
axis: binary search over a large sorted array — latency-bound unpredictable access plus one data-dependent branch per probe

name: fill-sum
axis: hot-loop element write + read on a pre-allocated i32 array; per-access bounds-check cost

name: matmul
axis: 2D matrix multiply over flat row-major arrays — cache behaviour on a 3-deep loop nest plus the per-access bounds check on the innermost read/modify/write

name: push-growth
axis: growth by push — geometric-reallocation amortization plus the push fast path

name: reverse-inplace
axis: in-place reverse — two cursors walking toward each other; 2 bounds-checked reads + 2 bounds-checked writes per iteration with no arithmetic to hide them behind

name: sort-heap
axis: sort — HAND-WRITTEN heapsort, the same algorithm in all four; branchy, cache-hostile random access over a large array

name: struct-aos
axis: array-of-structs traversal — read 2 of 4 i32 fields from every record; the A side of the AoS/SoA layout A/B

name: struct-soa
axis: struct-of-arrays traversal — the same records held as 4 parallel scalar arrays; the B side of the AoS/SoA layout A/B

name: map-i32
axis: i32-keyed hash map: insert, hit/miss lookup, iterate (VL's dedicated mono key rep)

name: map-string
axis: string-keyed hash map: insert, hit/miss lookup, iterate

name: set-ops
axis: hash set: build two overlapping string sets, then intersection / difference by membership test

name: struct-alloc
axis: GC pressure — allocating and discarding many short-lived heap structs (binary-trees shape)

name: struct-array-scan
axis: array of structs scanned by field — memory layout (inline records vs array of references)

name: struct-field
axis: struct field read/write in a tight loop — flat, then two levels of nesting

name: word-freq
axis: mixed map + string: tokenize a synthetic corpus and count word frequencies (read-modify-write upsert)

name: ackermann
axis: Ackermann — the densest call-overhead stress available: nested recursive calls in argument position, nothing memoizable or strength-reducible

name: deeprec
axis: deep LINEAR NON-TAIL recursion (5_000 live frames per call) — stack depth + return-path cost

name: fib
axis: naive binary (non-tail) recursion — raw call/return overhead with a near-empty body

name: flatcall-inlined
axis: the CONTROL for flatcall — identical loop with the leaf function's body written out at the call site

name: flatcall
axis: static direct call to a tiny leaf function, 1.2e9 times — the CALL half of the call-vs-inline pair

name: mutual
axis: MUTUAL recursion — two functions calling each other, 800 levels deep; the cross-function-call cycle no compiler can inline its way out of

name: tailcall
axis: TAIL-position linear recursion at depth 5_000 — does the runtime eliminate the tail call?

name: treewalk
axis: recursion over a REAL recursive heap structure — pointer-chasing binary tree, built recursively then walked recursively

name: char-scan
axis: per-character read throughput over a long ASCII string

name: concat-build
reason: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT: cross-language ratio is unusable. The Rust column measures NOTHING — min-of-7 pinned wall time is 4.6ms, BELOW the 6.8ms empty-Rust-program startup baseline. deno reads 56.0ms (34% launcher) and python3 71.5ms (17% launcher); VL reads 1730ms. No REPS value fixes this: work is linear in REPS for Rust/JS/Py but VL is O(n^2) in N and linear in REPS, so REPS x20 puts Rust at ~92ms (still under the 200ms floor) and VL at ~34s. The VL-INTERNAL finding survives and should still be reported: doubling N multiplies VL by ~3.5x (O(n^2)) while Rust/JS/Python stay ~1.6-1.9x (O(n)) — VL's `s = s + c` reallocates and copies both operands every append. Do not publish any Rust/JS/Python-vs-VL multiple from this directory.
